root_cause.text: thermal_of_cm_lookup() in the thermal/of subsystem leaks a device tree node reference because the struct device_node * returned by of_parse_phandle() is not released with of_node_put() after comparison.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message explicitly state that “tr_np is obtained via of_parse_phandle(), but never released,” and the patch fixes this by changing tr_np to `struct device_node *tr_np __free(device_node) = of_parse_phandle(child, "trip", 0);`, adding automatic cleanup for the leaked reference.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use scoped automatic cleanup for `tr_np` in the cooling-map lookup loop to avoid leaking device node references from `of_parse_phandle()`.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration for `tr_np` was changed from an uninitialized `struct device_node *` declared separately to a single declaration initialized with `of_parse_phandle(child, "trip", 0)` and annotated with `__free(device_node)`.
intent_record.how: This makes `tr_np` automatically released when it goes out of scope on each loop iteration, preventing leaked device node references while preserving the existing lookup logic and control flow.

commit 423de5b5bc5b267586b449abd1c4fde562aa0cf9
Author: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Date:   Fri Feb 21 17:57:11 2025 +0100

    thermal/of: Fix cdev lookup in thermal_of_should_bind()
    
    Since thermal_of_should_bind() terminates the loop after processing
    the first child found in cooling-maps, it will never match more than
    one cdev to a given trip point which is incorrect, as there may be
    cooling-maps associating one trip point with multiple cooling devices.
bic_trace_step.reason: The added function `thermal_of_cm_lookup()` contains the vulnerable construct described in the root cause. Inside the loop, it does `tr_np = of_parse_phandle(child, "trip", 0);` and then immediately compares `if (tr_np != trip->priv) continue;` without any corresponding `of_node_put(tr_np)` on either the non-match path or the match path. Because `of_parse_phandle()` returns a referenced `struct device_node *`, failing to release `tr_np` after comparison leaks the node reference. The function body is sufficient to determine this because the full relevant acquire/use/release logic is visible, and there is no `of_node_put(tr_np)` anywhere in `thermal_of_cm_lookup()`. The commit fixes unrelated loop control behavior in `thermal_of_should_bind()` by moving the lookup into `thermal_of_cm_lookup()`, but it does not include the required reference release fix.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in this snippet, especially in `thermal_of_for_each_cooling_device()` and related helpers, so the code is sufficient to decide. The root cause is leaking a DT node reference returned by `of_parse_phandle()` when it is only used for comparison and not released. In `thermal_of_for_each_cooling_device()`, the code does `tr_np = of_parse_phandle(map_np, "trip", 0);` and then uses it in `trip_id = of_find_trip_id(tz_np, tr_np);`, but there is no `of_node_put(tr_np)` on either the success path or error paths before returning. That matches the vulnerable construct exactly: a node acquired from `of_parse_phandle()` is not released. By contrast, other parts of this same snippet show the expected pattern, e.g. `of_node_put(cooling_spec.np);` after `of_parse_phandle_with_args(...)` in `__thermal_of_bind()` and `__thermal_of_unbind()`, which highlights that the missing put for `tr_np` is not intentional. Therefore the function contains the reference leak and does not yet contain the fix.
